members.reason: [llm] duplicates #2555: Both PRs fix the same underlying bug: MCPError (and subclasses, notably UrlElicitationRequiredError) is not pickle-safe. The default Exception.__reduce_ex__ reconstructs via cls(*self.args), but self.args is set to (code, message, data) by MCPError.__init__, which doesn't match subclass constructor signatures - e.g. UrlElicitationRequiredError takes (elicitations, message). This is tracked as issue #2431.

members.title: fix: don't send a response for cancelled requests
members.author: Zelys-DFKH
members.reason: [llm] duplicates #2514: Both PRs rewrite `RequestResponder.cancel()` in src/mcp/shared/session.py to fix the same defect: when an in-flight request is cancelled, the session currently sends back an error response, which violates the JSON-RPC/MCP cancellation contract (the peer should get a `notifications/cancelled`, not a response). #2493 removes the erroneous error-response-send call in `cancel()` and updates the matching comment/log in server.py's `_handle_request` (leaving cancellation silent). #2514 touches the same `cancel()` method (adjacent lines, same function) and instead wires in an actual `notifications/cancelled` send (new `CancelledNotificationParams` import) covering both the request-timeout and caller-cancellation trigger paths, and drops the `# pragma: no cover` marker on the `_entered` guard, indicating the branch is now exercised by new tests.
